title: Lagerphone (bottle-cap pole)
summary: The lagerphone is an Australian bush instrument: a wooden pole studded with flattened bottle caps threaded loosely on nails. Shaken, struck with a stick and stamped on a board it jingles and thumps to keep time for bush bands, and it can be made from almost nothing.
howToPlay: The pole stands on its stamping board: the crown of caps at the head, rows of caps down the shaft.
Top is the crown, Upper, Middle and Lower the rows of caps down the pole, and Stomp the board under the foot.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Strike as it lands.
Begin with the stomps and the middle rows, then add the crown.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The patterns count four beats to the bar.
heritageNote: Players of the bush bands made lagerphones from broom handles and the caps they had at hand. The player stamps the foot on a board for the bass beat while the caps ring on the pole, so one person can keep the whole band in time.
credits: Tradition: the Lagerphone; patterns written for this game
